extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians considering submitting a research article to the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and journal-level criteria for authors preparing and deciding whether to submit original research articles to the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, including scope, peer-review model, open-access options, and related-journal fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and quality standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes articles of the highest quality and significance across a broad range of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should submit work that constitutes significant advances in mathematical knowledge; the Proceedings is the Society’s high-impact flagship journal and expects papers of very high quality. (Implied: ensure results are significant and of wide interest within mathematics.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Page length policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no page length restrictions for submitted papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are not constrained by a maximum page limit when preparing submissions to the Proceedings; prepare the manuscript at the length needed to present the work fully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles published in this journal are peer reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted manuscripts that proceed to publication will undergo peer review. However, editors may desk-reject without external review (see next criterion). Authors should prepare manuscripts to professional standards for external peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial desk-rejection policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may reject papers without external review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial team may decide at submission that a manuscript is not suitable for external review (e.g., outside scope, insufficient significance, or not meeting standards). Ensure fit to journal scope and quality before submitting to reduce risk of immediate rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review model — identity transparency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal uses a single-anonymised review process (i.e., typically the reviewers are anonymous). Authors should prepare submissions consistent with this model (e.g., do not rely on open identities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer communication channel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers communicate via the editor rather than directly with authors; correspondence and revisions are handled through editorial channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of review information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal does not publish peer review reports or reviewer identities; authors should not expect public disclosure of review history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access model and options
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication model: Hybrid open access. The journal has options for gold and green open access publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default articles are subscription-based but authors may choose gold OA (presumably via APC) or green OA routes. Authors must check and select the appropriate OA option if required by funders or institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funder/institution open access compliance check
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting to the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, authors should check any open access requirements from their institution or funder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an author is required to publish open access but cannot identify a compliant route with the journal, they should contact the journal team before submitting to resolve compliance options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match to related-journal scope and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Related publications have different emphases: the Bulletin publishes concise articles reporting significant advances, survey articles and obituaries; the Journal of the London Mathematical Society publishes longer articles reporting significant advances; the Transactions is fully open access and publishes across the full range of mathematics; the Journal of Topology is dedicated to high quality and significance in topology, geometry and adjacent areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should choose the most appropriate LMS journal based on specificity, length, and disciplinary scope — e.g., concise/significant work or surveys to the Bulletin, longer significant advances to the Journal, broad-range or specialist items to Transactions, and topology/geometry-focused high-quality work to Journal of Topology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance production step
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, it will be sent to the publisher for typesetting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be prepared for publisher-led production (typesetting) after acceptance; check journal guidance for production timelines and queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to read submission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting an article to the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, we recommend that authors read the submission guidelines for the Proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the journal's full submission guidelines (formatting, LaTeX templates, submission system instructions, author responsibilities) to ensure compliance and avoid procedural delays.
